notes: Changed rule, graded against the current text: Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call. git diff 3e3581d -- idiomatic-elixir/ rewrites its first paragraph; the sentence that now decides the verdict is "Unless a call's result is bound to a name, each of its arguments is a name or a short literal: a map, struct or keyword list that would span several lines is built first under a name that says what it is, one field per line, with a blank line between multi-line statements." with its new exemption "A call whose result is bound to a name may take its options inline, as `formatter` does below". No run has a call bound to a name that takes multi-line options inline, so the exemption decides nothing here, and the "passed on, matched against, nested in another call or discarded" sentence covers every :ets.new/2 call (all are discarded or returned). Violating runs: 0 of 5; 2026-10-22-c had 1 of 5 (sonnet-2, inline six-line :ets.new/2 options).

Every call whose argument is a map, struct or keyword list, per run. Opus-1: :ets.new(name, table_options) (line 141), named first at lines 133-139, one field per line, blank line 140; its match specs are named on one line (in_window line 98, expired line 124); MyApp.Application builds rate_limiter_options on one line (line 201) and children over lines 203-208 before Supervisor.start_link(children, strategy: :one_for_one, name: MyApp.Supervisor) (line 210). Haiku-1: :ets.new(name, table_options) (line 139), named at lines 131-137, blank line 138; its match specs are inline one-line lists (lines 121, 145), short one-line literals as 2026-10-22-c graded haiku's. Haiku-2: :ets.new(name, @table_options) (line 119) with the options a one-line module attribute (line 66); match specs inline on one line (lines 156, 160). Sonnet-1: :ets.new(name, table_options) (line 132), named at lines 124-130 with blank lines around; a multi-line match spec named match_spec (lines 165-174, blank line 175, call line 176) and a one-line named one (line 181). Sonnet-2: both :ets.new/2 calls take one-line literals (line 89 :ets.new(name, [:named_table, :public, :ordered_set, write_concurrency: true]); line 91), the shape 2026-10-22-c graded clean for haiku-2's line 108; its match specs are named (line 67) or inline on one line (line 105). The moduledoc or comment child lists are built under children in every run that shows one; the haiku-2 moduledoc tuple wrapped over lines 24-25 is inside the docstring and not counted, as 2026-10-22-c left haiku-1's. Each run wrote ratelimit.ex with one Write (sonnet-2 after a first heredoc), and the final file is byte-identical to that Write, so mix format moved nothing.

The other nine listed rules have unchanged text since 3e3581d (the diff also touches the reference-file table row for ex_unit.md, the new Formatting bullet under How to use this skill, the do: rule, Before you finish step 1, and testing.md renamed to ex_unit.md with the Assert with patterns edit; none is on this case's list, and processes.md is unchanged) and are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-22-c/grades/rate-limiter-skill.json: an if on one boolean condition is clean; a single fallible call handled with a case whose success clause returns the next step's result is clean under the with rule, which also covers haiku-1's read_limits/1 -> decode_limits/1 -> parse_limits/1 chain of such cases (lines 159-171); a two-step with whose body returns a third fallible call is not counted (haiku-2 lines 169-172 and sonnet-2 lines 114-117 returning parse_config/parse_limits); a run with no with and no fallible {:ok, _} | {:error, _} call is not exercised (sonnet-1, whose load_limits!/1 raises at boot through File.read!/1 and JSON.decode!/1); key, id, acc, other, decoded and similar local names are not counted under Naming, and no run uses a single-letter name; section-label comments and commented start-up and caller examples (opus-1 lines 214-216, sonnet-2 lines 154-204) are not counted under Comments, as 2026-10-22-c graded baseline-sonnet-2's; reading the limits file in init/1 is a missed case check but decides no verdict, because the responsive rule names only HTTP calls and large queries as slow work; sonnet-2's limits table name :"#{name}.limits" (line 79) is built from the start option, not from user data, as 2026-10-22-c left it.

Designs. All five keep one ETS row per admitted request in a public ordered_set table owned by a GenServer; the caller inserts its row, counts with :ets.select_count/2 and deletes its row when over the limit; a handle_info/2 sweep deletes expired rows (opus-1 and haiku-1 every 10 s, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 every 60 s). Limits live in :persistent_term keyed by the instance name (opus-1), as rows in the same table (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1), or in a second, protected table (sonnet-2). So Pick the abstraction, Use ETS, Keep each process behind one module and the call/cast and per-key cleanup parts of the responsive rule are clean in all five, and every start_link/1 accepts :name. Every run reads the limits file inside init/1: opus-1 line 109 (File.read/1 at line 156), haiku-1 line 107 (line 160), haiku-2 line 117 (line 169), sonnet-1 line 133 (File.read!/1 at line 191), sonnet-2 line 86 (line 121). All five read JSON with the built-in JSON module. Only opus-1 compiles its start-up and caller examples as modules (MyApp.Application, a plug and an Oban worker); haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 show callers in the moduledoc, sonnet-2 in comments after the module.

Verification, in scratch copies under grade-d-rate-limiter-skill. All five pass mix format --check-formatted; the only lines over 98 characters are in the moduledoc (sonnet-1 line 34) or a comment (sonnet-2 line 170). Haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors; opus-1's full file fails at import Plug.Conn (line 228) because its example plug and Oban worker need Plug and Oban, while lines 1-192 (the limiter) compile alone with --warnings-as-errors. In every run a 50-task concurrent burst admitted exactly 2 for user 1 at the default limit of 2 and 5 for user 42, configured at 5; a second instance under name: :other kept its own count (2 of 50); an injected 61-second-old request row was removed by one :sweep message and the other rows kept. Opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 key counts by to_string(user_id), so 7 and "7" share a count; sonnet-1 looks the limit up by to_string(user_id) (line 150) but keys counts by the raw id (line 147), so 7 and "7" each got the full limit.

All five runs have rc 0 and a model_id matching their tier, and their skill_hash, 1fd3c153a1dee8f91ed580b1911b8d65aa5569f39ec08a9ab9c8ec3e336326b3, equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/ (run head ba24972, uncommitted false; git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/ is empty).
